items.text: I’ll build the secure notes app, save the prompts and evidence, and prepare the submission documents and recording script. I’ll commit in clear stages: scaffold, working app, security checks, then submission materials.

I’ll use a Flask and SQLite notes app with separate user accounts, private notes, and a small interface that’s easy to demonstrate. I’m also using the Documents and PDF skills to build and visually check the homework report.

The scaffold is committed and pushed on `codex/hw6-secure-notes`. The app now has registration, login, private note editing, CSRF checks, and server-side session revocation; the login page loads successfully. Next I’m checking whether a second account can read, change, or delete another user’s notes.

The full create, read, edit, delete, and sign-out flow passed its smoke check, and the working app is committed and pushed. Canvas shows Homework 6 is due tonight at 11:59 p.m. I’m now testing the security boundaries and preparing the recording steps.

All 59 security tests pass, including account isolation, CSRF rejection, HTML escaping, SQL injection attempts, and replaying a signed-out cookie. The checks also caught two error-handling bugs with hostile hostnames and oversized note IDs; both are fixed. That stage is committed and pushed.

The dependency audit found no known vulnerabilities in the pinned runtime packages, and the app works in Chrome. I’m assembling the report and recording script next. The remaining student step will be the narrated recording with your camera on initially; I’ll leave its URL blank until there’s a real video.

items.text: I’ll read Homework 6 and check our Lab 6 context for anything that carries over.

Yes—I found your Lab 6 work: Python authentication, password hashing, tests, and the Flask guestbook with its CSRF fix. **Homework 6 directly builds on those coding-agent skills.**

According to the [assignment](https://icardei.github.io/gensec-web/labs/G06.3_hw_wk6/index.html), we need to:

- Build a working **Python application using prompts to a coding agent**, and identify the agent.
- Save the development prompts in `hw6/prompts.txt`, with the application in `hw6/app.py`.
- Address security issues caused by adversarial input.
- Capture readable screenshots of the prompts and agent replies.
- Push the code and prompts to your course repository.
- Record a **narrated screencast of five minutes or less**, starting with your camera on: clone the repository, explain the prompts, replay generation, explain security, and demonstrate functionality and limitations.
- Submit a PDF containing the screenshots, repository URL, and recording URL. The instructions specify an **unlisted YouTube recording**.

**My recommendation is a secure notes application built with Codex:** login, private notes, SQLite storage, password hashing, CSRF protection, and input validation. It connects naturally to Lab 6 and gives us clear security demonstrations that fit the recording limit.

The key planning detail is the **replay from scratch**: we should keep the generation prompts short and reproducible from the beginning.
